rows.name: Koopa Troopa (green shell turtle enemy, walks left)
rows.notes:
World 1-1's Koopa Troopa, paused at 16-bit level x = 1652 (page $006E+1 = 6, low $0087+1 = 116), screen origin (16,185) with the camera at x 1638; it faces and walks LEFT (every OAM entry has flip_h set). PROOF: list_sprites (paused, game_mode $0770 = 1) decodes a 6-entry OAM group at slots 40-45 whose drawn pixels are one 16x24 metasprite, all sprite palette 5 (attr $41 -> palette bits 1, no behind-background bit). Cross-checked in RAM: enemy object slot 1 is active ($000F+1 = 1) and its type byte $0016+1 = $00, while the two Goombas in the same frame are slots 3-4 with type $06 - a different enemy type. OAM entries as (tile id, x/y offset from the origin (16,185), flips):
- $A5 (165), (+0,+0), flip_h - head, top-left (rounded dome: $27 orange index-3 outline, $30 white index-2 centre, a $1A green index-1 stripe)
- $FC (252), (+8,+0), flip_h - blank filler; the head occupies only the left 8px column (the direction it faces), so the top-right cell is empty
- $A7 (167), (+0,+8), flip_h - shell, left half (nearly solid $27 orange index-3 with a $1A green index-1 edge)
- $A6 (166), (+8,+8), flip_h - shell, right half (diagonal hatch alternating $1A green index-1 and $27 orange index-3, with a $30 white index-2 spot)
- $A9 (169), (+0,+16), flip_h - lower-left foot/leg ($1A green, $30 white and $27 orange wedges)
- $A8 (168), (+8,+16), flip_h - lower-right foot/leg ($30 white/$1A green/$27 orange - a foot with a green sole)
So the metasprite is 16 wide x 24 tall: head row (2 cells, 1 drawn), shell row (2 cells), feet row (2 cells). Sprite palette 5 live = [15,26,48,39] = [$0F black, $1A green, $30 white, $27 orange]; get_region object mode at (20,196) returned 213 connected sprite palette-5 pixels using slots 1,2,3 across OAM #58,#60,#61,#62,#63 (CHR $A5,$A6,$A7,$A8,$A9), box (13,186)-(28,208). Found with no reference by playing right from the World 1-1 start (checkpoints: save slots 3 and 4 in this session); the Koopa is past the four pipes and the pit, just before the brick rows with the hidden 1-UP.
rows.why: the green Koopa Troopa walks left at the screen's left edge in this screenshot; OAM $A5 (head) with a $FC filler, $A7/$A6 and $A9/$A8 (shell and feet), all h-flipped: rendered from sprite CHR they are the Koopa facing left, 16x24

rows.name: flagpole shaft (left column)
rows.notes: Left of the two 8px background columns that make the World 1-1 flagpole's shaft. read_tile CHR $1A2: a single index-1 pixel column at the tile's RIGHT edge (col 7) and nothing else. Placed in the live nametable as tile id $A2 in the column immediately left of the pole line, running from under the ball down to the ground block. Together with CHR $1A3 (the same 1px line at ITS left edge, col 0) the pair $A2|$A3 side by side puts both 1px lines on the shared boundary, i.e. one 2px vertical green line - which is how SMB draws a thin pole with 8px tiles. BACKGROUND pattern table $1000 (background_pattern_addr 4096), BG palette 0, slot 1 = $29 lime green. PROOF: get_region color mode at (109,100) returned 128 pixels of background-palette-0 slot 1 across background CHR 0x1A2 and 0x1A3, box (108,68)-(109,131) - a 2px-wide vertical run - and reported NO other pixel in view uses that slot, so on this screen palette-0 slot 1 is the pole alone. get_tile_at_pixel (104,50) and (104,150) both returned tile_id $A2 / chr_tile $1A2 / palette 0 / screen_box (101,48) and (101,144); (112,100) returned $A3 / chr_tile $1A3 / screen_box (109,96). The pole's base block is nametable tile $AC (CHR $1AC) under it at (101,200), palette 1.
rows.why: the flagpole with its ball and the flag at its foot by the castle in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as one-pixel lines at the right and left tile edges (the 2-pixel shaft), $12F/$13D as the two halves of the ball, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant with its emblem

rows.name: flagpole shaft (right column)
rows.notes: Right of the two 8px background columns that make the World 1-1 flagpole's shaft, i.e. the mirror of CHR $1A2. read_tile CHR $1A3: a single index-1 pixel column at the tile's LEFT edge (col 0) and nothing else. Placed in the live nametable as tile id $A3 in the column immediately right of the pole line, from under the ball down to the ground; the shared boundary between the $A2 and $A3 cells is where the 2px green line appears ($A2's line is at its right edge, $A3's at its left edge). BACKGROUND pattern table $1000, BG palette 0, slot 1 = $29 lime green. PROOF: the same get_region color mode at (109,100) that returned the 128-pixel, 2px-wide run (box (108,68)-(109,131)) lists background CHR 0x1A2 AND 0x1A3; get_tile_at_pixel (112,100) returned tile_id $A3 / chr_tile $1A3 / palette 0 / screen_box (109,96), and (112,150)-region cells carry the same tile down the shaft.
rows.why: the flagpole with its ball and the flag at its foot by the castle in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as one-pixel lines at the right and left tile edges (the 2-pixel shaft), $12F/$13D as the two halves of the ball, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant with its emblem

rows.name: flagpole ball (left half)
rows.notes: Left tile of the ball that caps the World 1-1 flagpole. read_tile CHR $12F: a rounded blob whose content sits in the tile's RIGHT columns (cols 5-7) - index-2 body, index-3 outline, one index-1 highlight column - i.e. the right side of a circle, so placing it one tile left of the pole centre completes the ball's left half. Placed as nametable tile id $2F at the very top of the pole, directly above the shaft columns; BACKGROUND pattern table $1000, BG palette 0 (slot 1 $29 lime green highlight, slot 2 $1A green body, slot 3 $0F black outline). PROOF: get_tile_at_pixel (107,40) returned tile_id $2F / chr_tile $12F / palette 0 / screen_box (101,40), with the shaft tile $A2 directly below it; (104,34) above it is the blank tile $24, so $2F is the topmost pole graphic. Paired with CHR $13D at screen (109,40).
rows.why: the flagpole with its ball and the flag at its foot by the castle in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as one-pixel lines at the right and left tile edges (the 2-pixel shaft), $12F/$13D as the two halves of the ball, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant with its emblem

rows.name: flagpole ball (right half)
rows.notes: Right tile of the ball that caps the World 1-1 flagpole, the partner of CHR $12F. read_tile CHR $13D: a rounded blob whose content sits in the tile's LEFT columns (cols 0-3), index-2 body with an index-3 outline, flat edge at col 0 - the left side of a circle. Placed as nametable tile id $3D immediately right of $2F, so the pair $2F+$3D forms one green ball centred on the pole's 2px line; BACKGROUND pattern table $1000, BG palette 0. PROOF: get_tile_at_pixel (110,42) returned tile_id $3D / chr_tile $13D / palette 0 / screen_box (109,40) while (107,40) returned $2F - the two cells are adjacent at the same tile row, and $A3 (right shaft column) sits directly beneath $3D. Together $2F (content cols 5-7) + $3D (content cols 0-3) span screen x 106-112, centred on the pole line at 108-109.
rows.why: the flagpole with its ball and the flag at its foot by the castle in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as one-pixel lines at the right and left tile edges (the 2-pixel shaft), $12F/$13D as the two halves of the ball, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant with its emblem

rows.name: flagpole flag (the pennant that slides down the pole)
rows.notes:
The flag on the World 1-1 flagpole at the end of the level - it is a SPRITE, not background: it rides the pole down when Mario grabs it, and in the frame inspected (Mario had already slid) it sat at the bottom of the pole just above the ground. PROOF: get_region object mode at (105,175) returned 136 connected sprite-palette-5 pixels using slots 1 and 2 across OAM #10, #11, #12 (CHR $7E and $7F), box (93,172)-(108,187) = 16x16. list_sprites decodes those three entries - all sprite palette 5 (attr $01 -> palette bits 1, no behind-background bit), no flips, drawn from the SPRITE pattern table $0000. Origin (93,172) = top-left of the 16x16 box; entries as (tile id, x/y offset from origin):
- $7E (126), (+0,+0) - upper-left: read_tile $7E is a solid index-2 right triangle (row 0 full width, each row losing one pixel from the left), the flag's $30 white field
- $7F (127), (+8,+0) - upper-right: read_tile $7F is an index-1 ($1A green) square carrying an index-2 ($30 white) ring/circle emblem
- $7E (126), (+8,+8) - lower-right: the same white triangle, giving the pennant its lower edge
(the lower-left cell is empty - that is what makes the flag a pennant rather than a rectangle)
Sprite palette 5 live = [15,26,48,39] = [$0F black, $1A green, $30 white, $27 orange]; the flag uses only slots 1 and 2. Its y is not fixed: it is set by the flagpole slide, so use the OAM offsets above (they are relative) rather than absolute screen coordinates. Reached with no reference by playing to the end of World 1-1.
rows.why: the flagpole with its ball and the flag at its foot by the castle in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as one-pixel lines at the right and left tile edges (the 2-pixel shaft), $12F/$13D as the two halves of the ball, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant with its emblem

rows.name: World 1-1 end: flagpole + flag + castle
rows.notes: The last screen of World 1-1. Contents: the eight-step staircase of brick blocks rising to the right, a short green pipe at its foot, the flagpole standing on a single base block (nametable tile $AC, CHR $1AC, palette 1) on the ground, with the castle to the right. THE FLAGPOLE IS BACKGROUND: the shaft is background CHR $1A2 + $1A3 (nametable tiles $A2|$A3 side by side, one 2px green index-1 line on their shared boundary), capped by background CHR $12F + $13D (nametable tiles $2F|$3D) forming one green ball on the pole, all BACKGROUND pattern table $1000 in BG palette 0 with slot 1 = $29 lime green. THE FLAG IS A SPRITE: sprite CHR $7E and $7F (OAM #10 tile $7E (+0,+0), #11 tile $7F (+8,+0), #12 tile $7E (+8,+8), origin (93,172), 16x16 box, sprite palette 5, no flips) - it slides down the pole when Mario grabs it, so its y is not fixed. Proof frame: paused just after the slide, camera scroll_x low byte 251 in nametable 0, the pole line at screen x 108-109, the ball at screen y 40, Mario at screen x ~154 walking toward the castle. Background palette 0 here = [$22 periwinkle sky, $29 lime green (pole + hills), $1A green, $0F black].
rows.why: World 1-1's end: the flagpole, the castle and the score 2000 for the flag, as the scene says (a side scene; the line is already promoted)

rows.name: $00CE rising past 176 and wrapping is the DEATH animation, not a pit - and $079F=200 makes the level-end run safe
rows.notes: Two lessons from playing World 1-1 to the flagpole with no reference. (1) Don't read $00CE (player_y, 176 = standing on 1-1's ground) as 'fell in a pit' too quickly: when Mario dies he does one small hop (apex ~123) and then falls straight through the floor, so the byte climbs past 176 and wraps 255->0 forever while his x freezes (that freeze is what made him look 'stuck against a wall'). Four separate 'falls' at level x ~1249, ~1527, ~1783 and ~2024 were all Goomba deaths, not holes: reading the nametable ground rows (PPU $2340/$2740/$2B40/$2F40, rows 26-29) showed full ground tiles $B4/$B5/$B6/$B7 across every column, with no gap anywhere. Real walls (pipes, staircase) block movement but do NOT raise $00CE; enemy deaths raise it. (2) The reliable way through a level full of enemies is the star timer at $079F rather than clever jumping: write_memory CPU $079F (decimal 1951) = 200, then a single play_input run of ~600 frames with a jump tap cycle carries Mario ~1100 px with no deaths and no life lost. The timer decrements ~1 per 20 frames, so 200 covers ~4000 frames (several runs). Confirm it is still live by watching $079F in play_input's watch list.
